text.insert: Every workflow in this feature — run, PR campaign, sync — is its own state machine, and this page defines what they share. The common envelope makes every durable state object readable by the same machinery; ProjectState composes those objects into the general state of the system; the dispatch lease decides which workflow may act on it. The operator action inventory at the end is what the UI projects from this state.
Common State Envelope

Run, PR campaign, sync, and session state are separate objects with separate status vocabularies, but the system has to order, trace, block, and display all of them the same way. The envelope is the shared layer that makes this work — every durable state object carries the same four things:

text.insert: Exactly zero or one workflow holds the dispatch lease — the token that allows it to dispatch worker agents and mutate its allowed checkout surfaces. Background worker-result ingestion may continue regardless, because it consumes immutable evidence and never dispatches workers or touches the checkout.

props.title: Decision (2026-08-12) — ProjectState shows every workflow; "foreground" becomes active workflow + dispatch lease

text.insert: The canonical project object is ProjectState, whose session, run, PR, and sync slots stay present so all three workflow states exist durably at once. Only the dispatch lease is exclusive: exactly one active workflow may use it to dispatch worker agents and mutate its allowed checkout surfaces.
Why Only the Lease Is Exclusive
ProjectState keeps a slot for every workflow because all three exist durably at once; exclusivity lives in the dispatch lease alone:
foreground lease → dispatch lease.
foreground workflow → active workflow.
project.foreground_* events → project.dispatch_*.
The retired foreground vocabulary implied the opposite — that inactive workflows stopped existing between activations — which is why it is gone. The old names map one-to-one onto the new:
Canonical Project State
ProjectState is the top of the state tree: one object per project that answers what exists and who may act.

props.description: Canonical project state: the session, one always-present slot per workflow, the dispatch lease, background knowledge, and trace summary.

fields.name: revision
fields.description: Monotonic state version used for ordering and stale-write protection.

fields.name: session
fields.description: Active session identity and head. The SessionState object is canonical.

fields.name: run
fields.description: Always-present run slot: the current run's identity and status, mirrored for at-a-glance reads. The RunState object is canonical. Null only when no run exists in the session.

fields.name: pr
fields.description: Always-present PR slot mirroring the open campaign. The PrCampaignState object is canonical.

fields.name: sync
fields.description: Always-present sync slot mirroring the current or requested sync. The SyncState object is canonical.

fields.name: active_workflow
fields.description: The workflow currently holding the dispatch lease — the token that allows it to dispatch worker agents and mutate its allowed checkout surfaces. Null when no workflow is active; run, PR, and sync states all remain durable either way.

fields.name: lease_id
fields.description: Fencing token minted at acquisition; every worker-dispatch and source-mutation command must present the current lease id, so stale actors from a previous activation are refused.

fields.name: requested_handoff
fields.description: Queued transition that begins after the current owner settles.

fields.name: blockers
fields.description: Reasons the owner cannot settle or release authority.

props.title: Decision (2026-08-12) — two-tier confirmation and an explicit sync publish gate

text.insert: confirmation_required is true exactly when an action is outward-facing or irreversible: it pushes anything upstream, discards work, or is terminal. Sync rests at validated until the operator triggers its confirm-gated publish action.
Confirmation and Publish Mechanics
The rule is a single test — confirmation_required is true exactly when the action is outward-facing or irreversible:

Everything else — pausing, resuming, draining, starting sync, entering PR work, recording a manual save point — is a single click gated only by blockers. Routine controls the operator hits constantly must never nag; the blocker list, not a dialog, explains when they are unavailable.

Sync adds the one deliberate stop in the system: after validation passes it rests at validated, and only the operator's confirm-gated publish action crosses the point of no return. Upstream movement while it rests surfaces as a staleness blocker with re-validation available. The matrix below is the full v1 inventory; its Confirm column applies this rule.

props.title: Operator action inventory (v1)

text.insert: The domain object supplies everything else: its own status enum and its own payload. That split is what keeps the machinery generic — ordering, stale-write protection, blocker display, and trace lookup are written once against the envelope, while each workflow page defines only its vocabulary and shape. A new state kind joins the system by wearing the envelope, not by teaching every consumer about itself.
Identity — id, project_id, and kind — names every object the same way, so a run, a campaign, a sync, and a session are addressed uniformly by every consumer.

Ordering is one rule everywhere: revision increments once per accepted transition, and caused_by_event_id names the event that produced it, which is what makes stale-write protection and history reconstruction generic.
Blockers share one shape, so any surface can explain why any object is stuck without knowing its domain.
The trace anchor (trace_id) ties every object into the same tracing fabric as its events and operations.
A PR campaign in review does not stop existing while a run executes, and a requested sync is real state before it ever acquires the lease — so every slot stays visible.
The lease is the sole grant of the right to dispatch worker agents and mutate checkout surfaces, and exactly one workflow may hold it at a time.
Because one-at-a-time is lease policy rather than structure, the desired future run + PR concurrency is a policy change, not a reshape of ProjectState.
It composes the active session and one slot per workflow — run, PR, and sync — where each slot mirrors just the identity and status of a workflow object that stays canonical for its own detail.
The active_workflow field carries the dispatch lease; when it is null nothing may dispatch, and every workflow state remains durable and visible either way.

The lease is enforced by fencing, not trust: a lease_id is minted at each acquisition, and every worker-dispatch and source-mutation command must present the current one, so a stale actor from a previous activation is refused rather than obeyed.
There is deliberately no universal status enum — each workflow owns its vocabulary on its own page, and ProjectState only mirrors those values.
Outward-facing: publishing a PR batch or the sync boundary pushes work upstream where reviewers see it, and published work cannot be quietly unpublished.
Work-discarding: cancelling a sync, abandoning a campaign, or hard-stopping a run throws away real work the operator may not mean to lose.
Terminal: cancelling a run, closing a campaign or session, or breaking a lease through recovery cannot be undone afterward.
